source_title: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 8 July 2026 (Digital Omnibus on AI)
summary: The Digital Omnibus on AI was published in the Official Journal of the European Union on 24 July 2026 as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) together with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 (civil aviation) and Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (machinery). It enters into force on 27 July 2026, the third day following publication. From that date the deferred deadlines are enacted law: Annex III standalone high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027, Annex I product-embedded high-risk obligations from 2 August 2028, Article 50(2) watermarking for existing systems from 2 December 2026, and the new Article 5 prohibition on AI-generated CSAM and non-consensual intimate imagery from 2 December 2026. Article 50 transparency duties for new systems keep their 2 August 2026 date, unchanged.
mechanical_change: Regula's OMNIBUS_OJ_DATE flipped to 2026-07-24, deriving the in-force date 2026-07-27. Applicable deadlines in reports, registration packets, explanations and timelines now carry the deferred dates as current law, with the pre-Omnibus dates kept as history and all in-force wording date-qualified ("in force from 2026-07-27") so nothing overstated legal status during the three days between publication and effect.
verified_by: EUR-Lex ELI record retrieved 2026-07-27 (automated fetch of eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng returned the regulation text): confirms Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026, OJ 24 July 2026, entry into force on the third day following publication (recital 46), Annex III deferral to 2 December 2027 and Annex I deferral to 2 August 2028 (recital 40, quoted), new Article 5 points (ba)/(bb) prohibitions, amended Article 11(1) SME/SMC simplified documentation, and the four-month marking transitional period for providers on the market before 2 August 2026 (recital 38). Previously corroborated by two independent specialised legal publishers (EU Law Live, 24 Jul 2026; NicFab). The retrieval was automated; a maintainer eyeball of the EUR-Lex page remains a cheap extra assurance step.
